lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Clarify the target role and create targeted versions for product and operations or strategy applications.
items.because: The mix of mechanics, logistics, product work, an MBA and student ventures makes the career direction unclear.

items.says: Explain the transition between business or product work and the current mechanic role.
items.because: A product recruiter may wonder why the current job is mechanical.

items.says: Reorder the experience roles or separate relevant and additional experience.
items.because: The internship appears after an earlier full-time role, so the current order is not reverse-chronological.

items.says: Make the overlapping MBA, internship, project and employment dates clearly compatible.
items.because: The overlaps may raise questions about the chronology.

items.says: Distinguish MBA projects from professional employment.
items.because: Recruiters evaluate academic projects and employment differently.

items.says: Prioritize relevant sections and experience for each target role.
items.because: Strong product evidence is diluted by operational and mechanical experience.

items.says: Reduce page density by prioritizing the strongest outcomes.
items.because: The content will fit on one page only if formatted efficiently, and the Harbor Payments bullets are dense and overlapping.

items.says: Make the LinkedIn URL a clickable, professional link.
items.because: The displayed format looks generic or incomplete.

items.says: Clarify that the MBA is completed if applying after June 2025.
items.because: Its end date has passed and it should not appear ongoing.

items.says: Add a concentration only if it supports the target role.
Consider adding a relevant leadership role, competition or academic distinction.
items.because: It should strengthen the candidacy.

items.says: Explain this role’s relevance to business or product applications, or place it in Additional Experience.
items.because: It creates a major question about career direction after the MBA.

items.says: Give this role more prominence and technical detail for mechanical or industrial operations applications.
Define what “under 5 days” measures and provide a previous baseline if available.
items.because: Without context, the dry-dock achievement is difficult to evaluate.

items.says: Add the number of jobs completed if substantial.
items.because: Fleet size alone does not show individual throughput.

items.says: Give non-marine readers enough context to understand “dry-dock time.”
items.because: The term may not be understood by the target audience.

items.says: Replace or shorten the responsibility-only maintenance bullet in a product or business-focused version.
items.because: It is weaker than the outcome-based bullet above it.

items.says: Add the scale of the systems, vessels, inspections or records handled.
State the inspection, compliance or regulatory outcome.
items.because: The bullet does not say whether inspections passed, finished on time or met a requirement.

items.says: Communicate the breadth of this role beyond its analytical title.
items.because: The bullets also show program management, process improvement, stakeholder management and vendor ownership.

items.says: Explain what owning the scorecards involved.
items.because: “Owned” is vague.

items.says: Replace the meeting description with its decisions or business impact.
items.because: It describes meeting logistics rather than an accomplishment.

items.says: Add the number of carriers, regions, managers or shipments covered.
Clarify the baseline and measurement period for the 30% reduction.
items.because: The result is more credible when readers know whether it occurred over one month or one year.

items.says: Explain “pick errors” for general business readers if needed.
items.because: The term may be clear only to logistics employers.

items.says: Define S&OP on first use for generalist recruiters.
Specify the forecast-error measure and what was forecast.
Consider cutting the 12-quarter duration if space is tight.
items.because: The result is more important.

items.says: Separate or trim the accomplishments packed into this bullet.
items.because: The tool rollout, procedures, training and vendor negotiations make it dense.

items.says: Explain how the 1,800 saved hours were calculated and validated.
Clarify how the telematics contract relates to the driver-hour savings.
items.because: The causal link is not fully clear.

items.says: Keep the internship near the top in a product-focused version.
items.because: It is more relevant than the mechanic role and possibly the logistics role.

items.says: Represent an intern’s responsibility level accurately.
items.because: Company-wide launches and roadmap decisions could overstate ownership.

items.says: Clarify whether you designed the onboarding solution or contributed with design and engineering.
items.because: The bullet does not establish your personal role.

items.says: Indicate that the single verification step retained required controls, if relevant.
items.because: The change may raise compliance or risk questions.

items.says: Confirm that all 2,300 merchants were measured in the pilot and that the comparison is valid.
Specify that the conversion lift is five percentage points rather than five percent.
items.because: The distinction matters.

items.says: Define the scope of “all merchants.”
items.because: It is a very broad rollout claim.

items.says: State the roadmap decision or business outcome of the RICE prioritization.
items.because: The bullet is mostly a process statement.

items.says: Explain whether support tickets were a valid proxy for affected users or an intentional internal measure.
items.because: The meaning of Reach needs to be precise.

items.says: Consider combining this with the next roadmap bullet.
items.because: The two may describe the same process.

items.says: Specify what roadmap priority changed and what happened afterward.
items.because: “Set the next quarter’s roadmap priority” is vague.

items.says: Clarify whether leadership approved the recommendation, a feature was built or a measurable reduction followed.
items.because: The bullet does not establish the decision’s significance.

items.says: Make the decision easier to identify amid the many listed activities.
items.because: The sequence can obscure its significance.

items.says: Explain or verify why session-level randomization was appropriate.
items.because: The same user might encounter both experiences.

items.says: Distinguish the unit of analysis, experiment population and affected party.
items.because: Calling the result an effect on merchants’ customers may be imprecise.

items.says: This bullet repeats the earlier checkout-conversion accomplishment.
items.because: It adds no distinct business outcome.

items.says: Specify what leadership “funded.”
items.because: It could mean a budget, engineering capacity or formal rollout authorization.

items.says: Update “Present” if the project or app is no longer active.
Clarify whether this was an operating product, student venture or classroom project.
items.because: The distinction affects how recruiters evaluate the results.

items.says: State the current level of involvement if the project continues.
Consider moving this project above less relevant experience in a product application.
items.because: It provides valuable product evidence.

items.says: Define what the 3,100 students represent.
items.because: They could be registered users, eligible students, notified students or total reach.

items.says: Clarify the two dining halls’ role.
items.because: “With two dining halls” does not say whether they used the app or supplied food.

items.says: Explain whether the nine tonnes were weighed or estimated.
items.because: The measurement needs verification.

items.says: Give the start and end of the app’s first year.
items.because: The measurement period is unclear.

items.says: The stated 150% increase is incorrect; 400 to 1,150 is a 187.5% increase.
items.because: The calculation is an important credibility issue.

items.says: Clarify the periods used for the before-and-after weekly-active-user comparison.
Verify the implied causal link between the interviews and the reminder decision.
items.because: “Chosen after 60 user interviews” implies the interviews directly established the feature choice.

items.says: Calling the move from 75% to 95% a 20% increase uses the wrong type of change.
items.because: It is 20 percentage points, or approximately 26.7% relative increase.

items.says: Clarify whether the volunteer shifts were a product intervention, an operational process or both.
Add the fill-rate measurement period.
Make the practicum’s academic context clear.
items.because: Its dates overlap with the MBA.

items.says: Distinguish personal contributions from the team’s work.
items.because: “Team Lead” alone does not establish the individual contribution.

items.says: Keep the $2.4 million clearly identified as modeled, forecast or validated savings.
items.because: “Sized” suggests an estimate rather than realized savings.

items.says: Add the implementation timeline, adoption status or pilot budget if known.
items.because: That would make the client outcome more concrete.

items.says: Rewrite the passive bullet to emphasize impact rather than work performed.
items.because: It primarily describes mapping and shortening a form.

items.says: Quantify the improvement in form length, intake time, errors or staff burden.
items.because: No measurable improvement is given.

items.says: Clarify whether all four clinics adopted the changes and how adoption was established.
items.because: Adoption may have been formally approved or merely observed.

items.says: Make the individual role in mapping or redesign clearer.
Avoid duplicating the pilot approval described in the financial-impact bullet.
items.because: Both bullets may describe the same approval process.

items.says: Clarify whether the pilot launched or was only approved.
items.because: Approval should not imply implementation.

items.says: Make the product skills section less short and generic.
items.because: It is underdeveloped for a product-management application.

items.says: Consider separating discovery, experimentation, analytics and delivery skills.
items.because: The categories would be more specific if supported by the experience.

items.says: Ensure “A/B testing” is supported by sound experiment-design knowledge.
items.because: The session-level randomization and measurement bullets raise questions.

items.says: Specify the artifacts meant by “requirements writing.”
items.because: The skill is broad.

items.says: Add relevant demonstrated capabilities such as forecasting, stakeholder management or financial modeling.
items.because: The experience shows capabilities missing from the skills list.

items.says: Develop the tools list with other substantively used, relevant tools if applicable.
items.because: The current list is underdeveloped.

items.says: Ensure listed tools are supported by experience elsewhere.
items.because: Recruiters may test proficiency.

items.says: Pair Excel with specific analytical or modeling capabilities if possible.
items.because: Excel alone may be less differentiating.
